title: Electron electric dipole moment and missing CP violation
bottleneck: The Standard Model contains far too little CP violation to explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe, so physicists hunt for new sources. The electron electric dipole moment is a pristine probe: any nonzero value above the Standard Model's tiny prediction would reveal new CP-violating physics. The ACME collaboration has pushed the bound down by orders of magnitude and still finds nothing.
why_it_blocks: Without discovering where the missing CP violation hides, explanations of baryogenesis remain speculative. The null results constrain supersymmetric and extended-Higgs models so tightly that whole classes of theories are ruled out, yet the asymmetry they were meant to explain remains a fact in need of a mechanism.
current_state: The latest ACME measurement sets the most stringent limit on the electron electric dipole moment to date, with next-generation molecular-fountain and trapped-ion experiments aiming to improve sensitivity further. Theorists are increasingly pushed toward models where new CP violation sits at very high energy scales.
